No, as far as I know most of the official plugin collabs are with Japanese plugin devs like Triacontane and Sasuke Kannazuki.
To address your tangent about me personally: I was interested in Chrono Engine and did a lot with it but eventually got into GDevelop instead as it's a much more flexible engine suitable for that type of gameplay while also regularly getting first party support and updates. It's also FOSS so anyone can submit code to be included in the official build or fork it and make their own spinoff engine (e.g. Carrot Engine). RPG Maker being a specialized engine is particularly good at making (2D turn based) RPGs and saves you a lot of work if that is the type of game you want to make at the cost of flexibility.
There is a business model difference here: GDevelop makes money through (optional) subscriptions for cloud services so there is a regular income stream, and they can indefinitely keep updating one engine. RPG Maker makes money through the initial engine sale and asset pack DLCs, this has to keep releasing new engines to keep the money coming in, or convert to a subscription model.

posts.body:
Going back to the topic, I would suggest to someone with sufficient disk space use the kind of tool that downloads everything including attachments, then with said content (which will be seen as HTML, but attachments will be there), build a new forum, and manually add a library of kind of resources, which is also backed on a
private
github where every contributor coordinates.
Exclusions should the categories of paid/etc content, like for example, paid comissions, or articles from stuff that are for sale in the RPGM store.
What I'm suggesting is essentially what "Way Back Machines"-like does, but with the difference that attachments will also be kept, and some exclusions are also placed.
NOTE: Content not directly attached to posts (like mediafire links etc) shouldn't be downloaded, so the required space will be much smaller.
And, the new forum should have a resource to allow removal requests of authors that didn't wanted their content to be kept.
What is more important is the private github, there is where people can coordinate for the new forum, and there should be at least a minimum of ten managers accepting/revoking join requests, plus some people checking if the uploaded content is right.
For the public forum, add two subcategories for each category: one where only the staff members (with collaborator roles) can open topics which needs approval from higher staff member before become visible for every user, and the other subcategory completely open for the community, with an attached topic saying the rules and "request rules to get old content back".
Lastly, the new forum should have a feature to transfer ownership, so an original author can request the ownership of the topics published on "subcategory A", and then, after transfer the ownership, transfer the topic to "subcategory B".
And, for less hassle,
the links of the topics should be in numerical format  being the category/subcategory not added on the link (global link format)
(i.e: forums.rpgmakerweb.com/topic/2039348)
, so if someone transfer a topic, or changes topic name, anything, the links won't break. Same for commentaries (i.e: link.com/topic/203938#021393 or link.com/comment/3299848)
Things like this is what we should discuss.
Hope that my suggestions helps you to coordinate a proper solution to keep all content.
